newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen seen going higher as rate fears ease.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen seen going higher as rate fears ease.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures rebounded on Tuesday, partially reversing for the first time big losses triggered by comments by Japan's "Mr Yen" last week.
Dealers said the rally, which had pushed June Euroyen futures up 10 ticks to a high of 99.19 in late trade, reflected a market view that the recent sell-off had been too dramatic.
"Last week was overdone," said a Singapore-based dealer with a U.S. bank.
June Euroyen fell from an intra-day high of 99.22 on November 7 to a low of 99.05 the next day after comments by senior Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara.

Sakakibara, dubbed Mr Yen by the media because of his ability to influence the Japanese currency, said the Japanese economy was stronger than the market thought and that he thought the yen's recent fall was over.

The comment sparked rumours of a Japanese interest rate rise -- either to stem inflationary pressures or to prop up the yen -- and brought the U.S. dollar crashing down from over 114 yen to a low of under 111 on Tuesday.
But dealers said the market had now dismissed as highly unlikely an imminent rise in Japanese rates.
"There is no reason to raise rates," said one dealer.

"What possible benefit would the Japanese government get from that? Governments love low bond rates because it means they can repay their debts at cheap rates," said the dealer. "And the Japanese economy is hardly overheating."
Dealers said the June Euroyen contract could go up to around 99.20/.25, which would still be below its high of 99.30 seen on October 30. September 1997 Euroyen could get back to 99.13/.14.
June Euroyen stood at at 99.19 by 1130 GMT, up 10 ticks and against its previous IMM settlment at 99.10. September Euroyen was at 99.03, up 13, and against its IMM settle at 98.91.
December JGB futures rose 0.56 to 124.07, after opening at 123.63.
Eurodollar futures were seen as range-bound with little impetus after the closure of U.S. markets on Monday due to the Veteran's Day public holiday.
"There's little or no mileage in Eurodollars as long as U.S. rates look unlikely to change," said another dealer.
The March 1997 Eurodollar contract closed up two ticks at 94.47, against its IMM close at 94.45.
